Hello I have a lot to say, cuz its me and I'm extra. I will say, that I know some of the stuff I will mention is already being addressed but its still worth mentioning. As always this game is a lot of fun and I respect the amount of work put into it. The people, DMs, mods, and players are what keep this game interesting and enjoyable. The amount of times I tell my irl friends about this game is ridiculous, I always have a story to tell whenever I play here with y'all. That being said, I want to be transparent about some issues, of course there can never be a perfect game but I wanted to provide some feedback. So here we go

Things I loved: 
• The arcaniabot was amazing: props to Roy 
• The long rest thing actually made me take brakes from playing and also was motivation to wake up the same time as my player (I know in season 3 I would play literally all night) 
• I loved being able to learn the gun prof. 
• The crafting was cool, I still struggled with it but that's nothing new, 3 years in a row and crafting has always been kinda hard for me to grasp. I've only ever understood the season 2 version
• The chance to create a new form of government and debate it. It drove me crazy but I loved it. Being able to shape world we are apart of in multiple ways is really cool
• Running with character choices, running npcs, quests we choose to work with
• Shoutout to Radar for all the fun little chaos moments, giving us laughs and things we love to hate (Vanderbuilt)


The break and inactiveivity:
• The DMs didn't end the break at the expected time so it was 2 weeks long
• The amount of active players cut down 
• Even if there were no encounters or interactions from DMs we still could have done things like planned player/mod ran events, I wanted to have a shooting competition for example but it felt like I couldn't organize it
• We could have done crafting, learning a skill or something that felt like we were progressing throughout the break

Running the game:
• Encounter balance was rough, maybe have a mod or someone dedicated to balancing because some things were too much (hence so many deaths) 
• Would have liked to see more communication between DMs. 
• Encounter conditions should not be based on rounds before pcs can move on that will only make combat take hours. Waiting a specific # of pc turns is more predictable no matter how many people are in init (Hampstead bomb event) 

Other things:
• Maybe have a chat dedicated to planning that is separate from ooc so information doesn't get lost
• I like risk with death, this season if felt like death was more of a means for transformation rather than risk. I understand it was created this way as a response to the events of season 3, but the motivation and weight that came from those who went through the hatch was also some of my favorite moments. Maybe find balance between the two?

If the creature is undead, roll the 5d12 damage if the damage would kill it, it crumbles to dust instead of giving it temporary hit points. You can use this once per day and it resets at the witching hour. 

Once per week you can thrust the diseased spirit of the Uru upon a creature to truly Harm (DC17) them.


The Spellmart: The soft white root radiates with a calming and warm presence. you can press the staff to the ground and cast Circle of Power. When cast this way, the staff holds the concentration of the spell and all friendly creatures within the circle gain temporary hit points equal to their proficiency bonus. You can use this once per day and it resets at dawn.

Once per week, at your bequest, can extend and solidify it’s warm presence into a Globe of Invulnerability. 

The Baeshra Tree: The hearty roots of the Baeshra tree are brimming with wild and ancient powers. By your will these powers can surge into you and you become a Guardian of Nature. When cast this way the staff holds the concentration the Guardian forms get the following changes:
Primal Beast: Your appearance becomes more lizard like and the bonus damage die becomes a d8.
Great Tree: The temporary hit points refresh each turn, as long as the spell is active.
You can use this once per day and it resets at dusk.

Once per week you can wield the power of the Baeshra Tree to Reincarnate a deceased creature, however they only reincarnate as a Lizardfolk.

The staff can be split apart into 3 separate staves: The Hanging Staff, The Spellmart Staff, and the Baeshra Staff. When split the staves lose their ability to use their weekly ability and only give a +1 bonus to saving throws, save DC, and spell attack bonus.

A rumor of a new ferryman.

Bo had lived his life as one grand adventure, one of new beginings. After a time in a city, where death had become fuzzy and muddled... where the souls of the dead had begun to rise again. Bo had made a descision. The dead need to rest. Their time has come, and the balance must be upheld.

 Upon one's death, a shadowy figure appears near the dying person. A slow and melodical lullaby played on a banjo herolds the coming of death, and eases the soul. It beckons the pain to evaporate away, and bring peace to the dying's mind. 

A flash of light in your final moment, the life you lived played out before you, is met with a curious looking ethereal pseudodragon giggling as it boops your nose. The now dead, finds themself ridng a few feet above the river styx, on a flying carpet. 

To whatever language you speak, or what ever form you take, there is one on the carpet with you. As a changling in life near the end, he appears as one of your own race, to help comfort you as he delivers you to the afterlife.

"Well howdy there fella!" He greets you with a warm smile.
"We got a ways ta go, how about you be tellin me your name, mine's Bo! And this here's Lucy" the pseudodragon waves from his shoulder.

If a person is near death, but there time has not yet come... The shadowy figure would still appear and play the lullaby, and your life would still flash before your eyes. But that person... would wake up in the land of the living still. The only image they would remember from their near death experience, Lucy booping their nose. A moment would pass before the living would soon forget the giggling pseudodragon, as she beamed across the sky leaving a rainbow in her wake.

This is the grandest adventure of Bo Harkness, now a true captain of his vessel. To comfort the dearly departed, making friends with all he transports. To listen to your life's story.
